blogs.title: From Massive Models to Tiny Tweaks: The Quest for Parameter‑Efficient Finetuning
blogs.description: Large foundation models can contain billions of weights, making it practically impossible to train them from scratch for most researchers. Parameter‑efficient finetuning lets you adapt these giants to new tasks with only a few hundred or thousand extra learnable parameters, preserving the wealth of knowledge they already contain. This post explains why such techniques are now indispensable for practical AI.

blogs.title: Angle Matters: How Orthogonal Finetuning Preserves Knowledge
blogs.description: Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT) rewrites a weight matrix by multiplying it with an orthogonal matrix, guaranteeing that the angles between neurons stay the same. This property keeps the semantic information captured during pretraining intact while allowing the model to specialize to a downstream task. The article breaks down the math behind OFT and why preserving angles is so effective.

blogs.title: Fast Fourier Meets AI: Butterfly Factorization Makes Orthogonal Finetuning Feasible
blogs.description: The butterfly structure, famously used in the Cooley‑Tukey FFT, allows a dense orthogonal matrix to be expressed as a product of many sparse orthogonal matrices. This factorization reduces the number of trainable parameters from quadratic to linear‑logarithmic in dimension, while still being able to generate a dense transformation. We explore how this insight turns OFT into a parameter‑efficient method called BOFT.

blogs.title: Beyond Diffusion: BOFT Across Vision, Language, and Generative Models
blogs.description: BOFT is not limited to controllable text‑to‑image diffusion. Experiments show that it can adapt large vision transformers, language models, and diffusion models to a variety of downstream tasks with fewer parameters and better generalization than competing methods. This post highlights the empirical results and explains what makes BOFT versatile.

blogs.title: What Makes BOFT Work? Expressivity, Spectral Stability, and Implicit Bias
blogs.description: Unlike simple low‑rank updates, BOFT’s butterfly‑factored orthogonal matrices preserve the spectral norm of pretrained weights and approximate a broad class of linear transforms. The structured inductive bias they impose leads to better training stability and generalization. The article dives into the theoretical guarantees and why a moderate increase in expressivity can still keep finetuning reliable.
